lines.text: StockX's 2020 revenue topped $400 million, without owning the shoes.
lines.say: StockX's twenty twenty revenue topped four hundred million, without owning the shoes.

lines.text: That came from about $1.8 billion of sneakers traded on its platform.
lines.say: That came from about one point eight billion dollars of sneakers traded on its platform.

lines.text: So what's the business? A middleman that inspects the shoes.
lines.say: So what's the business? A middleman that inspects the shoes.

lines.text: Entry-level sellers pay a 9% transaction fee plus 3% processing.
lines.say: Entry-level sellers pay a nine percent transaction fee plus three percent processing.

lines.text: Buyers then pay their own fees and shipping on top.
lines.say: Buyers then pay their own fees and shipping on top.

lines.text: Our math: on a $200 sale, the seller pays $24 in fees and keeps $176 before shipping.
lines.say: Our math: on a two hundred dollar sale, the seller pays twenty-four in fees and keeps one hundred seventy-six before shipping.

lines.text: Rivals are close: GOAT takes 9.5% plus a seller fee, eBay 8% on pairs of $150 or more.
lines.say: Rivals are close: GOAT takes nine and a half percent plus a seller fee, eBay eight percent on pairs of one hundred fifty dollars or more.

lines.text: By our math, StockX brought in over 22 cents per $1 traded in 2020.
lines.say: By our math, StockX brought in over twenty-two cents per dollar traded in twenty twenty.

lines.text: The real product isn't shoes. It's trust that they're real.

post.title: How StockX Hit $400M in Revenue Without Owning Shoes
post.ig:
StockX brought in over $400 million in revenue in 2020 without owning the shoes.
It matched $1.8 billion in sneaker trades that year and charged both sides.
Entry-level sellers pay a 9% transaction fee plus 3% processing (as of late 2026). Our math: a $200 sale leaves the seller $176 before shipping.
GOAT charges 9.5% plus a seller fee; eBay charges 8% on sneakers of $150 or more.
By our math, StockX brought in over 22 cents per dollar traded in 2020.
Sources: StockX April 2021 funding announcement and 2020 snapshot; StockX, GOAT and eBay fee pages (checked Nov 2026).
